inflation_annual.source: Average of BLS CPI-U headline (3.7%) and core (2.6%, all items less food and energy), both 12 months ending Sep 2026, released 2026-10-14: https://www.bls.gov/news.release/cpi.htm. Chosen over headline alone because energy-driven spikes (energy +20.4%) usually fade over a 24-month horizon; not pure core because bills include utilities. Headline-only would be 3.7%.

raise_annual.source: BLS Employment Cost Index, private-industry wages and salaries, 12 months ending Sep 2026 (released 2026-10-30): https://www.bls.gov/news.release/eci.nr0.htm

ss_cola_annual.source: SSA 2027 cost-of-living adjustment, determined 2026-10-14, first payable Jan 2027: https://www.ssa.gov/oact/cola/latestCOLA.html (2026 was 2.8%). The engine applies it on the as_of anniversary, not in January.

rent_renewal_bump.source: BLS CPI rent of primary residence, U.S. city average, 12 months ending Sep 2026: https://www.bls.gov/charts/consumer-price-index/consumer-price-index-by-category.htm. National figure; regional releases were higher (Midwest 4.1%), so check before publishing.

forecast_paths.source: Design choice: Monte Carlo paths per forecast; a 24-month run takes well under 100ms at this size.

job_loss_monthly.source: BLS CPS labor force status flows, employed to unemployed, seasonally adjusted: monthly flow divided by beginning-of-month employment. Average of Jun-Jul, Jul-Aug, Aug-Sep and Sep-Oct 2026 (0.78%, 0.93%, 0.89%, 0.96%), computed from the counts at https://www.bls.gov/web/empsit/cps_flows_recent.htm (modified 2026-11-06). Includes people who quit into unemployment, so it slightly overstates involuntary job loss.

reemployment_monthly.source: Chosen so the expected spell matches BLS mean duration of unemployment, 27.1 weeks (about 6.2 months), Oct 2026, Table A-12: https://www.bls.gov/news.release/empsit.t12.htm (1 / 6.2 = 0.16). The raw CPS unemployed-to-employed flow is higher (about 25% a month, 23.6-26.4% over Jun-Oct 2026) but averages over a mix of short and long spells, which understates a long job loss; the median spell is 11.9 weeks. A memoryless chain cannot match both, and a stress test should not be optimistic.

ui_replacement.source: Pennsylvania L&I: 'Your Weekly Benefit Rate should equal about one-half of your full-time weekly wage': https://www.pa.gov/en/agencies/dli/resources/for-claimants-workers/benefits-information/benefit-guide . Applied to gross pay and treated as take-home (benefits are taxable; withholding is optional).

ui_weekly_cap.source: Highest rate in the Pennsylvania L&I 'Rate and Amount' chart ($604/week): https://www.pa.gov/en/agencies/dli/resources/for-claimants-workers/benefits-information/benefit-guide/eligibility-information . The chart is undated, so the 2026 maximum is UNCONFIRMED (some secondary sources say $605). Check before publishing.

ui_max_months.source: Pennsylvania regular UC pays up to 26 times the weekly rate (18-26 weeks depending on credit weeks), about 6 months: https://www.pa.gov/en/agencies/dli/resources/for-claimants-workers/benefits-information/benefit-guide . Assumes the full 26 weeks.

emergency_fund_months.source: Design choice: 3 months of essential expenses is the common minimum rule of thumb; the formula takes the target as an argument (6 is typical for one-earner or variable-income households).
